items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: pop music like early Elvis, Jerry Lee Lewis, started to creep in

ctx.x: Yes. Mainly dancers at the various animal clubs like The Moose and The Elks and The Lions. You know. Things like that. And then we played for sock hops at the high school. We played for various things but we played the same tunes kind of over and over, “Tuxedo Junction” comes to mind, “In the Mood,” “Satin Doll” I think.
Was there a point during this band’s life where pop music like early Elvis, Jerry Lee Lewis, started to creep in and did you get requests for such things?

I remember eventually playing “The Green Door,” “I Ain’t Nothin’ But a Hound Dog” and then a little later “Tie a Yellow Ribbon Around the Old Oak Tree” or something. Now that’s about it but I’ll tell you, in the early 90s I just stopped playing — I stopped playing any job where they were smoking, number one. And number two I think the band leader that I was playing with, bass at one time, we played together for some years but he was branching out into what you’re talking about and some country tunes and things.…
